summary: The root جرف (jrf) signifies taking away or removing something entirely or in large part, often with force.
lane: 1 جَرَفَهُ جرف جرفه جرفة , (S, Msb, K,) aor. جَرُفَ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. جَرْفٌ (S, Msb, K) and جَرْفَةٌ , (Lh, K,) He took away, carried away, or removed, the whole of it, (S, Msb, K,) or the greater part of it, (S,) or much of it: (S, K:) and [in like manner ; for its inf. n.] تَجْرِيفٌ signifies the act of carrying away wholly: (KL:) and he took the whole of it. (TA in art. جفت .) -b2- Also, (inf. n. جَرْفٌ , TA,) He swept it away, namely, mud, (S, K,) from the surface of the earth; (TA;) and so , (K,) inf. n. تَجْرِيفٌ ; (TA;) and : (K:) or signifies the act of clearing away mud or the like well; in Persian, نيك رنديدن : (KL: [Golius, app. misled by a mistranscription, has explained the verb, جرّف , as on the authority of the KL, by “ bene effudit: ”]) and الشَّىْءَ he swept away the thing ( جَرَفَهُ ) from the surface of the earth. (TA.) You say also, جَرَفَتْهُ السُّيُولُ , (Msb,) or , inf. n. تَجْرِيفٌ ; (S;) and ; (S, K;) The torrents swept it away; (TA;) [or swept it partially away; or wore it away; ] namely, a portion of land. (S, Msb, K. See جُرُفٌ .) And, of a death commonly prevailing, جَرَفَ النَّاسَ كَجَرْفِ السَّيْلِ (tropical:) [ It swept away, or destroyed, men, like the sweeping away of the torrent ]: (TA:) and مَالَ القَوْمِ [ It sweeps away, or destroys, the cattle of the people ]. (S, TA.) -b3- [ He shovelled it, or scooped it, away, or up, or out. ] You say, جَرَفَهُ بِكِلْتَا يَدَيْهِ [ He scooped it up, or out, with both his hands ]; i. e. something dry, as flour, and sand, and the like. (S in art. حفن .) -b4- جُرِفَ It (herbage) was eaten up utterly. (TA.)

headwords.def: جَرَفَهُ جرف جرفه جرفة, (S, Msb, K,) aor. جَرُفَ, (S, Msb,) inf. n. جَرْفٌ (S, Msb, K) and جَرْفَةٌ, (Lh, K,) He took away, carried away, or removed, the whole of it, (S, Msb, K,) or the greater part of it, (S,) or much of it: (S, K:) and [in like manner; for its inf. n.] تَجْرِيفٌ signifies the act of carrying away wholly: (KL:) and he took the whole of it. (TA in art. جفت.) Also, (inf. n.

جرّفهُ جرف جرفه جرفة, inf. n. تَجْرِيفٌ: see 1, in four places. جرّفهُ الدَّهْرُ (assumed tropical:) Time, or fortune, or misfortune, destroyed, or exterminated, his property, or cattle, and reduced him to poverty.
اجرف أجرف اجرف جرف It (a place) was invaded by a torrent such as is termed جُرَاف. (K.)
تَجَرَّفَ see 1, in two places; and see جُرُفٌ.
إِجْتَرَفَ see 1, in three places.
جُرْفٌ جرف: see جُرُفٌ. Also A smooth side of a mountain. (A boo-Kheyreh, K.)
جِرْفٌ جرف: see the next paragraph.

جُرُفٌ جرف and, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) the latter a contraction of the former, (Msb,) [ An abrupt, water-worn, bank or ridge; ] a bank ( جَانِبٌ Ksh and Jel in ix. 110) of a valley, the lower part of which is excavated by the water, and hollowed out by the torrents, so that it remains uncompact, unsound, or weak; (Ksh ib.;) a bank, or an acclivity, of a water-course of a valley and the like, when the water has carried away from its lower part, and undermined it, so that it has become like what is…

جُرَافٌ جراف A torrent that carries away everything; (S, Msb;) i. q. جُحَافٌ applied to a torrent; as also; (K;) and a torrent that sweeps away that by which it passes, by reason of its copiousness, carrying away everything, and so applied to rain. (TA.) (tropical:) A very voracious man: (K, TA:) a man who devours all the food: (S:) one who eats vehemently, leaving nothing remaining. (M, TA.) (tropical:) A man who marries much, or often, and is brisk, lively, sprightly, or active; as also.
جِرَافٌ جراف: see what next precedes.
نَيْطَلٌ جَرُوفٌ نيطل جروف [ A capacious bucket: see 3 in art. نهز ]. (S in art. نهز.)
جُرَّافَةٌ جرافه جرافة: see مِجْرَفَةٌ.

جَارِفٌ جارف: see جُرَافٌ. Also (tropical:) A death commonly, or generally, prevailing, (S, K, TA,) that sweeps away, or destroys, ( يَجْتَرِفُ,) the cattle of the people. (S, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Plague, or pestilence.

جَوْرَفٌ جورف: see جُرَافٌ. Hence, as being likened to the torrent thus termed, (TA,) (tropical:) A quick, or swift, بِرْ َون [or hack, &c.]. (K.) And (tropical:) An ass; [app. meaning a wild ass, because of his swiftness.] (Sgh, K.) And, accord. to some, A male ostrich: (as in the K:) but this is a mistranscription for جَوْرَقٌ, with ق. (Abu-l-' Abbás, T, Sgh, L, TA.)
جَارُوفٌ جاروف: see جُرَافٌ, in two places. Also (tropical:) Greedy; having an inordinate desire, or appetite, for food. (K, TA.) And An (tropical:) unfortunate man. (K, * TA.)
مِجْرَفٌ مجرف: see مِجْرَفَةٌ. [Hence,] بَنَانٌ مِجْرَفٌ [ Fingers, or fingers' ends, ] that take much food. (IAar, TA.)

مِجْرَفَةٌ مجرف مجرفه مجرفة A broom, or besom; (K;) a thing with which mud is swept away from the surface of the ground: (S, * TA:) [applied in the present day to a shovel: and a hoe: and a rake: ] as also: vulgarly,; [now applied by many to a drag for dragging rivers &c.; ] of which the pl. is جَرَارِيفُ. (TA.)
مُجَرَّفٌ مجرف (tropical:) A man who has had his property, or or cattle, destroyed, or exterminated, and who has been reduced to poverty, by time, or fortune, or misfortune. (TA.)
مُجَرِّفٌ مجرف (tropical:) Lean, or emaciated. (M, TA.) [See what next follows.]

مُتَجَرِّفٌ متجرف (tropical:) A ram whose general fatness has gone; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) and so a camel. (TA.) Lean, or emaciated; as also مُتَجَلِّفٌ. (TA in art. جلف.) You say, جَآءَ مُتَجَرِّفًا (tropical:) He (a man, Ibn-'Abbád, TA) came in a lean and lax state ( هَزِيلًا مُضْطَرِبًا ). (Ibn-'Abbád, K.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
